title: SecOps Triage
voice_instructions: Warm, clear, confident technical product narration in natural American English. Speak at about 145 words per minute, with brief pauses between sentences. Avoid a sales pitch or exaggerated excitement. Pronounce SecOps as seck-ops, SIEM as seem, SDK as S D K, AWS as A W S, EC2 as E C two, EBS as E B S, and SSM as S S M. Read only the supplied text. Do not add words, music, or sound effects.

scenes.heading: From incident to a reviewable handoff
scenes.narration: Security analysts need more than another alert summary. They need the evidence behind the next decision. SecOps Triage turns an existing security incident into a reviewable investigation and handoff.

scenes.heading: One incident. One investigation.
scenes.subheading: Recorded local workflow  /  Synthetic evidence  /  Scripted provider
scenes.narration: Here, we select a reported phishing incident and start the investigation. This recording uses synthetic evidence and a scripted provider through the real Strands Agents SDK. No live model inference runs here.

scenes.heading: Real SDK calls. Inspectable evidence.
scenes.narration: Strands calls four scoped tools: inspect incident, look up entity, query activity, and find related cases. The trace shows nine actual evidence reads. Every result remains available for inspection.

scenes.heading: Similar messages. Different authorization.
scenes.subheading: Approval for the first message does not cover the follow-up
scenes.narration: The two messages look similar, but their identities and links differ. Authorization covers the first training message. The second was delivered and clicked, and a synthetic provider labels its exact link malicious. That approval does not transfer.

scenes.heading: Follow the citation. Keep the uncertainty.
scenes.subheading: Provider output, deterministic policy and final packet stay separate
scenes.narration: Open the cited source to inspect the evidence behind escalation. The interface separates provider output from deterministic policy and the final packet. A click alone does not establish stolen credentials, and unresolved questions stay visible.

scenes.heading: A durable handoff. An explicit next step.
scenes.subheading: Demonstration operator  /  Saved locally  /  Source SIEM unchanged
scenes.narration: The operator records missing context and a concrete next check, then saves an unresolved handoff. It is bound to this exact evidence packet. This demonstration record is local; the source SIEM stays unchanged.

scenes.heading: Framework, provider and host: explicit boundaries
scenes.subheading: Current UI: local  /  AWS service verification: completed separately
scenes.narration: Strands orchestrates the tools; the provider is scripted; host controls enforce scope, storage, and decisions. Separately, we verified a scripted run on AWS EC2, with encrypted EBS, SSM access, and CloudWatch delivery. That host is now stopped.

scenes.heading: Evidence first. Judgment stays with the analyst.
scenes.narration: The prototype passed three hundred ten tests. Scripted findings fail our completeness rubric; live-model evaluation and human usefulness remain unproven. SecOps Triage: evidence first, judgment with the analyst.
